claims.text: The page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ ('Output value errors') exists and covers this and other symptoms of treating a Pulumi output as if it were already a plain value.

In Pulumi, using an Output<T> as if it were a plain value (e.g., string conversion) produces placeholder text like 'Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported' in log lines, generated files, or resource properties.
A troubleshooting page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ covering errors from stringifying, branching on, or reading a Pulumi output value like a plain value.
Stringifying, branching on, or reading a Pulumi output value as if it were a plain value causes errors in Pulumi programs.
Pulumi Cloud returns a '409 conflict: Another update is currently in progress' error when another update is in progress on a stack.

The Pulumi CLI supports `--target` and `--exclude` flags to limit operations to specific resources.
Targeted updates can be used when a stuck or misbehaving resource is blocking a wider update.
Pulumi provides automatic logging, CLI verbose logging, and program logging for debugging and diagnostics, documented at /docs/iac/operations/debugging/logging/.

The logging guide at /docs/iac/operations/debugging/logging/ has an #automatic-logging anchor describing `pulumi logs share`.
Pulumi has a Community Slack at slack.pulumi.com that provides fast community support.

The page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ is the new update conflict page, replacing the #conflict section formerly on this page.
The logging page has a #cli-verbose-logging anchor for the verbose logging content formerly on the troubleshooting page.
Pulumi resource properties are represented as Outputs rather than plain values because their real values are not known until the providing resource has been created or updated.

When an output value is converted to a string directly (concatenated or logged) instead of via apply or an equivalent helper, Pulumi does not raise an error by default but silently substitutes a placeholder message in place of the value.
In TypeScript, converting an Output to a string yields literal text such as `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `apply` or `pulumi.interpolate`.
In TypeScript, calling `JSON.stringify()` on an output, or letting one flow into a JSON body, produces a `Calling [toJSON] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` string rather than the value.
In Python, converting an Output to a string via an f-string yields literal text such as `Calling __str__ on an Output[T] is not supported`, and Pulumi also logs a warning.
In Python, passing an output to `json.dumps()` fails with `TypeError: Object of type Output is not JSON serializable`.
In Python, `Output.json_dumps()` is the way to serialize an output to JSON.
In Go, passing a `pulumi.StringOutput` where a `string` is expected is a compile error, so static typing generally prevents the output-to-string mistake.
In Go, output values are resolved inside `ApplyT`.
In C#, converting an Output to a string yields literal text such as `Calling [ToString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `Apply` or `Output.Format`.
Setting the environment variable `PULUMI_ERROR_OUTPUT_STRING=true` makes converting an Output to a string throw an exception at the point of the mistake instead of returning placeholder text.
The `PULUMI_ERROR_OUTPUT_STRING` environment variable is supported in TypeScript, Python, and C# (not Go).

String-composition helpers for outputs are `pulumi.interpolate` and `pulumi.concat` in TypeScript, `Output.concat`/`Output.format`/`Output.json_dumps` in Python, `pulumi.Sprintf`/`pulumi.JSONMarshal` in Go, and `Output.Format` in C#.

A value read from an output inside an apply callback is only available inside that callback (or in outputs derived from it); the callback runs asynchronously, generally after the program's top-level code has finished, so an outer variable assigned within it is still undefined when read later.
The apply callback runs when the engine resolves the dependency graph, not on the program's clock, so adding a delay does not fix reading the outer variable.
Most resource inputs accept outputs as well as plain values, so an output can be passed directly as an input without apply.
A resource's logical name is a position that cannot accept an output.
In dynamically typed languages, an `if` on an Output evaluates the output object itself and is generally always true regardless of what the output resolves to.
In statically typed languages, branching on an `Output<bool>` is usually a compile error because an `Output<bool>` is not a `bool`.
Values known when the program starts, such as stack configuration read with `pulumi.Config`, environment variables, or hardcoded flags, are plain values and can be branched on normally.
Branching on `vpc.vpcId` with an `if` evaluates the Output object rather than its value, whereas using `vpc.vpcId.apply(...)` derives a new Output whose value depends on the branch.
Passing an output as a resource logical name, loop bound, or map key fails to compile in TypeScript, Go, and C#, where these positions are typed as plain strings or numbers.
In Python, passing an output as a resource's logical name raises `TypeError: Expected resource name to be a string`.
In Python, using an output as a loop bound (`range(some_output)`) raises `TypeError: 'Output' object cannot be interpreted as an integer`.
In Python, using an output as a dictionary key does not raise an error; Python falls back to comparing and hashing the output object itself, so the lookup silently keys on the wrong thing.

When resource names or counts depend on data known only after a resource is created, one fix is to provision dependent resources in a separate later stack that consumes the first stack's outputs through a StackReference.
A StackReference is documented at /docs/iac/concepts/stacks/#stackreferences.

Pulumi has no supported way to block the program and synchronously pull a resolved value out of an output; awaiting an output or reading it synchronously either doesn't compile, fails at runtime, or returns placeholder text.
Synchronous reading of outputs is deliberately unsupported because it would defeat building a dependency graph up front, since the engine would need the value before determining creation order.
`pulumi stack output <name>` reads a single stack output from the CLI after a deployment.
A StackReference from another Pulumi program consumes one stack's outputs as another stack's inputs.
The Automation API exposes an `outputs` field on the result of running an update (for example `res.Outputs` in Go).

The linked pages exist: /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/#outputs, /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/apply/, /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/all/, /docs/iac/concepts/stacks/#stackreferences, /docs/iac/concepts/automation-api/.
